speaker: Attorney
text: I want to move now to the afternoon of May 7, 2016. You told me earlier you were working the counter that day. What time did your shift start?

speaker: Witness D
text: I came in at noon. I was supposed to go until eight.

speaker: Attorney
text: And who else was working with you that afternoon?

speaker: Witness D
text: Nobody else on the floor. The manager had been in the morning, but she'd left by then. It was just me.

speaker: Attorney
text: You described the afternoon as slow. Can you give me a sense of how slow?

speaker: Witness D
text: Saturday afternoons it picks up around five, people coming back from the river or the lake. Before that it's maybe a customer every ten, fifteen minutes.

speaker: Attorney
text: Between, say, four o'clock and four-thirty, do you remember any particular customers?

speaker: Witness D
text: Not really particular. A man bought ice and gas. There was a lady who bought some things and went back outside. A couple of kids came in for drinks. That's about all I remember.

speaker: Attorney
text: The lady who bought some things and went back outside, did you know her?

speaker: Witness D
text: No. I didn't know her before that day.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you remember what she bought?

speaker: Witness D
text: Not exactly. A few groceries, I think. She had a bag.

speaker: Attorney
text: After she went back outside, did you see her again before you heard anything unusual?

speaker: Witness D
text: No. Once somebody goes out the door I can't really see them. Like I said, the windows are covered up.

speaker: Attorney
text: Okay. Let's talk about what you heard. At some point that afternoon did you hear something unusual?

speaker: Witness D
text: Yes. I heard a very loud bang. Really loud.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you know about what time that was?

speaker: Witness D
text: It was four-thirty-something. I remember because I'd just looked at the clock over the cooler, thinking about my break.

speaker: Attorney
text: Can you describe the sound for me?

speaker: Witness D
text: It was like a big crunch and a bang at the same time. Metal. It was louder than anything I'd heard out there, and you hear a lot of trucks on that road.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was it a single sound or more than one?

speaker: Witness D
text: The first one was the big one. Then there were some other sounds after, further away. Like scraping, and then another bang, further off.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: You can answer. Let me rephrase, actually. After the first loud sound, what else did you hear, in the order you heard it?

speaker: Witness D
text: After the big bang, there was a kind of scraping, crashing noise that kept going for a second or two. And then another thud a good ways off, east. Then it got quiet, except for the truck engine.

speaker: Attorney
text: How did you know it was a truck engine?

speaker: Witness D
text: You get to know the sound. Big diesel, idling. It was still running.

speaker: Attorney
text: Where were you when you heard the first bang?

speaker: Witness D
text: Behind the register.

speaker: Attorney
text: What were you doing?

speaker: Witness D
text: I was restocking the cigarette rack behind the counter. I had my back half to the front.

speaker: Attorney
text: From where you were standing at that moment, could you see the eastbound lanes of the highway?

speaker: Witness D
text: No. Not from back there. You can't see the road from the register.

speaker: Attorney
text: Could you see any part of the highway at all?

speaker: Witness D
text: Maybe a little sliver at the top of the door glass, but you're looking at the far side, and mostly you see the sky and the posters.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see the collision itself?

speaker: Witness D
text: No. I did not see it. I only heard it.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see either vehicle before the sound?

speaker: Witness D
text: No. I didn't see anything before the sound.

speaker: Attorney
text: What did you do after you heard it?

speaker: Witness D
text: I put down what I was holding and I went around the counter and out the front door.

speaker: Attorney
text: About how long did that take you, from the sound to getting outside?

speaker: Witness D
text: Not long. Ten seconds maybe. Fifteen. I wasn't running exactly, but I was moving.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: Is that your best estimate?

speaker: Witness D
text: That's my best estimate. It wasn't long.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you came out the front door, what's the first thing you noticed?

speaker: Witness D
text: The truck. You couldn't miss it. A big white truck with the long box trailer, stopped down 140th, past the store, on the south side.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you say down 140th, which direction is that from the store?

speaker: Witness D
text: South. 140th runs off the highway going south, right along the side of the store. The truck was down that road, past us.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was the truck moving when you first saw it?

speaker: Witness D
text: No. It was stopped. The engine was still running, like I said.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was the trailer still out across the highway when you came out?

speaker: Witness D
text: No. The whole thing was down on 140th by then. The back of it was past the store, sort of even with the back of the building, maybe a little further.

speaker: Attorney
text: Could you see whether the truck was on the pavement of 140th?

speaker: Witness D
text: It was on the road. I don't remember if it was all the way on the pavement or partly on the shoulder.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you notice anything about the trailer itself?

speaker: Witness D
text: The side of it was damaged. There was a long scrape and the bottom edge was torn up. I could see that from the front of the store.

speaker: Attorney
text: Which side of the trailer?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form. Foundation.

speaker: Attorney
text: If you know.

speaker: Witness D
text: The side facing the store, I believe. I was looking at it from the front of the store, so it would be that side, facing west and toward us. I'm not real sure which side you'd call that.

speaker: Attorney
text: That's fine. Did you go over to the truck?

speaker: Witness D
text: No. I didn't go to the truck.

speaker: Attorney
text: After you noticed the truck, what else did you see?

speaker: Witness D
text: I looked out at the highway and there wasn't a car anywhere near the intersection. And then I looked east and I saw the car way down, off the road.

speaker: Attorney
text: Off the road on which side?

speaker: Witness D
text: The south side. The same side as the store, just way down east.

speaker: Attorney
text: How far down would you estimate?

speaker: Witness D
text: Far. I'm not good with distances. A few hundred yards, maybe? It was down past where the fences are, in somebody's yard. Near a power pole.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: Do you know whether it was in a yard, or are you assuming that?

speaker: Witness D
text: I know the area. There's houses down that way with fenced yards. It looked like it was in one of those yards. I could see it had gone through a fence because the fence was down.

speaker: Attorney
text: Could you see the car clearly from in front of the store?

speaker: Witness D
text: Not clearly. I could see it was a dark car. I could see it was sitting there, stopped. That's about all from that far.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was there any vehicle traffic on the eastbound lanes at that point?

speaker: Witness D
text: Cars were stopping. A couple of cars pulled over on the shoulder. One stopped right out in the lane with its flashers on.

speaker: Attorney
text: And the westbound side?

speaker: Witness D
text: Some people slowed down, and I think one pickup pulled into the median crossover and stopped there. People were getting out.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you see anybody go toward the car down to the east?

speaker: Witness D
text: Yes, a couple of men from the cars that stopped went running down that way.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you go down there?

speaker: Witness D
text: No. I never went down there.

speaker: Attorney
text: Why not?

speaker: Witness D
text: I had the store. I couldn't just leave it open. And honestly, there were already people going, and I didn't think I'd be any help. I thought I should call.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you call anyone?

speaker: Witness D
text: I went back in and called 911 from the store phone. But they said they already had calls coming in, and they were sending people.

speaker: Attorney
text: About how long were you on that call?

speaker: Witness D
text: A minute or two. They asked where, and I told them the store at 140th and the highway. They asked if anybody was hurt, and I told them I didn't know, the car was way down the road and I hadn't gone down.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you then go back outside?

speaker: Witness D
text: Yes. Right away.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you went outside, either the first time or the second time, did you see anyone in front of the store?

speaker: Witness D
text: Yes. There was a woman out front of the store.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was that the same woman who'd been in earlier and bought groceries?

speaker: Witness D
text: I think so. I believe so. She had the same bag.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you notice her the first time you came out, or the second time?

speaker: Witness D
text: The first time, I really only looked at the truck and down the road. I think she was there, but I didn't really notice her until I came back out from calling.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you did notice her, where was she?

speaker: Witness D
text: Out front. Outside, out front of the store.

speaker: Attorney
text: Can you be any more specific than that?

speaker: Witness D
text: Not really. She was out front. I came out the door and she was right there, outside. I wasn't paying attention to exactly where.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was she standing or sitting?

speaker: Witness D
text: Standing, when I saw her.

speaker: Attorney
text: Can you describe how she appeared?

speaker: Witness D
text: She was really upset. She was crying and she had her hand over her mouth. She was shaking.

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Object to form.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'm only asking what you observed. Did she appear injured in any way?

speaker: Witness D
text: No. She wasn't hurt. She was just very shook up.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you go over to her?

speaker: Witness D
text: Yes. I went over and asked her if she was okay.

speaker: Attorney
text: I'm going to come back to your conversation with her in a moment. Before I do, I want to make sure I understand the scene. When you were standing out front, could you see the intersection itself, the crossover?

speaker: Witness D
text: Yes. From outside you can see the whole intersection. It's right there.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was there anything in the roadway at the intersection?

speaker: Witness D
text: There was some debris. Pieces of things, glass, some bits of metal or plastic in the eastbound lanes. Not big pieces.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did anyone move the truck while you were outside?

speaker: Witness D
text: No. It stayed where it was the whole time I was out there.

speaker: Attorney
text: And the car down to the east, did it change position?

speaker: Witness D
text: No. It stayed down there. Nobody moved it while I was there.

speaker: Attorney
text: About how long after the bang did the first deputy arrive?

speaker: Witness D
text: Maybe ten minutes. Maybe a little longer. It felt longer than it was, probably.

speaker: Attorney
text: Where did the first deputy go?

speaker: Witness D
text: The first car went right on past the store, down east to where the car was. Then the ambulance and a fire truck came, and they went down there too.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did any deputy come to the store?

speaker: Witness D
text: Later on, yes. A while after. One came up to the store and asked who had seen anything.

speaker: Attorney
text: We'll get to that. When you were standing out front with the woman, were there other people around the store?

speaker: Witness D
text: A couple of people came over. One man who had stopped his car came up and asked if we needed anything. And the kids who'd been in earlier were across the parking lot.

speaker: Attorney
text: Was the bench shelter you described earlier there that afternoon, in front of the store?

speaker: Witness D
text: Yes. It's always there. It was there.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did anything happen to the shelter in the crash?

speaker: Witness D
text: No. Nothing touched it. Nothing touched the store either.

speaker: Attorney
text: When you were outside, how long did you stay out front before going back in?

speaker: Witness D
text: I was in and out. I'd go in if somebody came in to buy something, which a few did, people who'd stopped. But mostly I was outside for the next hour or so.

speaker: Attorney
text: Let me go back to the moment you first walked out the door. I want to be precise. When you stepped out, was the truck already where you've described, stopped down 140th?

speaker: Witness D
text: Yes. By the time I got out it was already stopped there.

speaker: Attorney
text: So you never saw the truck moving that afternoon?

speaker: Witness D
text: Not before or after. I never saw it moving. Only stopped.

speaker: Attorney
text: And you never saw the car moving that afternoon?

speaker: Witness D
text: No. When I saw it, it was already down there and stopped.

speaker: Attorney
text: I know I asked this, but I want the record clear. Did you see the car and the truck come together?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Asked and answered.

speaker: Attorney
text: You can answer.

speaker: Witness D
text: No. I did not see it happen. I was inside behind the counter. I heard it, and then I went out and saw what I told you.

speaker: Attorney
text: Thank you. Now, when you went over to the woman out front and asked her if she was okay, did she respond?

speaker: Witness D
text: At first she couldn't really say anything. She was just shaking her head and crying. I put my hand on her shoulder.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did she eventually talk with you?

speaker: Witness D
text: Yes. After a minute or so, she started talking.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did she tell you her name?

speaker: Witness D
text: Her first name. And she said she was waiting on her sister to come pick her up.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did she tell you when her sister was coming?

speaker: Opposing counsel
text: Objection, hearsay.

speaker: Attorney
text: You can answer.

speaker: Witness D
text: She said her sister was supposed to be there around five. And her sister did come, a little before or around five, I think.

speaker: Attorney
text: Before the sister arrived, did the woman stay out front the whole time, as far as you know?

speaker: Witness D
text: As far as I know. She was out there whenever I was out there.

speaker: Attorney
text: Did you ever see her go down toward the car to the east?

speaker: Witness D
text: No. She didn't go down there. She stayed by the store.
